questions.question: Explain what resistance is in terms of electrons moving through a wire, and state its unit.
questions.expected_answer: As electrons flow through a conductor they collide with the vibrating atoms (ions) of the material, which opposes their flow; this opposition is resistance. Its unit is the ohm (Ω).

questions.question: A bulb is connected to a cell and a rheostat. Describe and explain what happens to the bulb when the resistance of the rheostat is increased.
questions.expected_answer: The total resistance increases, so the current decreases (the cell is the same), and the bulb becomes dimmer.

questions.question: Give two uses of resistors or of resistance heating, and explain why heating elements are made of nichrome rather than copper.
questions.expected_answer: Uses: limiting current to an LED; volume or dimmer control; LDR street lights; thermistors in thermostats; kettle, stove or geyser elements; filament bulbs. Nichrome has a fairly high resistance (so it heats up), a high melting point and does not oxidise when hot; copper has very low resistance, so it would barely heat.
